title: Booking Recovery Loop
summary: Recover stopped paid bookings with consent and delivery evidence.
user: Solo tutors, coaches, and consultants who sell paid sessions and need every abandoned or at-risk booking to become a completed, paid appointment. Paying customer: a one-to-five-person practice; wedge: conversion and delivery certainty after the booking link, at $29/month.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A tutoring side-hustle operator says scheduling tools feel bloated, clients get confused and text anyway; a legal consultant wants a booking experience that converts and includes Stripe.
A self-hosted Cal.com user reports that 24-hour and one-hour appointment reminder workflows were created but never executed.

recurrence: Independent solo-service complaints cover booking-page friction, payments, and reminder delivery; a missed paid session is immediately lost revenue.
current_workaround: Use Calendly/Cal.com plus Stripe plus manual texts, then check email logs when a reminder or booking goes missing.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly, Cal.com, SavvyCal, and Stripe solve calendar slots or payment individually. They do not make the conversion-to-attendance chain, including fallback recovery, the accountable product for tiny practices.
smallest_useful_product: Branded paid-session page, Stripe deposit, reminder delivery receipt, and an automatic SMS/email fallback when a booking is abandoned or a reminder bounces. Non-goals: calendar replacement, CRM, or marketplace discovery.
success_measure: In 60 days, pilot practices recover at least 10% of abandoned booking attempts or reduce paid-session no-shows by 20% versus their prior 60 days.
monetization: subscription — $29/month per practice is justified by recovering a single session and covers messaging delivery.
constraints: Obtain consent for SMS/email, use Stripe-hosted payment collection, encrypt client contact data, and support deletion/export.
why_distinct: The product owns measurable booking recovery and reminder proof, not just a public availability page.
